To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the application of FS and SFL to the analysis of transitivity patterns in two excerpts from the Harry Potter series reveals a clear power asymmetry between the two main protagonists, (ii) that the application of FS in particular highlights the role of perspective on an action as a key stylistic device, (iii) that FS and SFL complement each other, and (iv) that FS could be fruitfully applied to the analysis and teaching of literary texts, especially in combination with SFL

(a) the stylistic study based on the two theoretical models, FS and SFL, can provide a comprehensive and complementary account of the transitivity patterns in the two excerpts; (b) FS can be used as a stylistic tool for the description and analysis of literary texts; (c) the stylistic analysis based on the two models can help the reader understand the characters' evolution or involution in the two fragments.

(a) FS and SFL can be successfully applied to the analysis and interpretation of literary texts, and (b) the two models can be fruitfully integrated to enhance the descriptive power of stylistics, especially when dealing with fantasy literature.

the two approaches are complementary and that the integration of the perspective on an event into the SFL model of transitivity is a promising way forward.
the FS and SFL approaches are compatible, and can be fruitfully applied in tandem to the analysis of literary texts.

the two approaches, while not necessarily mutually exclusive, can provide complementary insights on the stylistic analysis and interpretation of a text.
